expected.summary: The Designer this tool started with session open, with nothing unsaved: it quits and its session is gone from the list. (Closing an instance a person started is dangerous and asks for confirmation.)

rows.reason: session close always closes the one instance it names; there is no call with nothing to close.

expected.summary: --discard is a switch and takes no value.
No running instance has that session ID.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.
The instance holds unsaved changes of this tool (schematic create not yet saved): refused with E_CONFLICT unsaved_changes; nothing closes.
Run under a scope file that does not grant the lifecycle effect; nothing closes.
While a long job of this tool runs in the instance: E_BUSY before anything else. --discard keeps the unsaved changes the job made from being refused first; nothing closes.
A person leaves a modal dialog open in the instance: E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with the dialog's title before anything else (--discard as in the busy row); nothing closes.
The connection breaks after Quit was sent and the process still runs.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Designer cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

rows.reason: This row applies only to a command that acts on a document.

The read-back is the session's absence from the list; the adapter's quit waits until the process is gone and fails with E_NATIVE_FAILURE or E_HUMAN_REQUIRED otherwise, so there is no stored value that can differ.
